clue.text: Going out once temperature's dropped for run is foolhardy

indicators.note: one letter is dropped and the other takes its place, a swap of letters in the word

parts.note: going out with someone means dating them
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone warns that heading outdoors once the temperature has fallen, to go running, is reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped for' swaps the T of DATING for an R.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe boldness that ignores danger; daring as an adjective is a near synonym of reckless or foolhardy.

clue.text: Opening half of Dame Kiri in recital is spirited stuff

indicators.note: the opening half of a four-letter word is its first two letters
in recital means spoken out loud, as in a performance

parts.note: the soprano Dame Kiri Te Kanawa; her first name said out loud matches the end of the cocktail's name

explanation.surface: Dame Kiri Te Kanawa opens her concert and the performance is lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening half of' gives DA from Dame; Kiri 'in recital', said out loud, matches the IQUIRI ending of the rum cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A daiquiri is a rum cocktail, and rum is a spirit, making it spirited stuff.

clue.text: Fancy dressing no good for this bird

indicators.note: no says the letter is to be left out

parts.note: robing is dressing in ceremonial or fancy robes

explanation.surface: A fancy-dress costume that fails to look like this bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from ROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: The redbreast is a common garden songbird, so this bird points to a familiar species.

clue.text: Dull time aboard to do with nerves

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so one letter is carried inside the other word

parts.note: neural means relating to nerves

explanation.surface: A boring time on board a ship that sets the nerves on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts T inside NEURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral colour is a muted, drab shade without brightness, so it is dull.

clue.text: Dreadful odds, with expert missing a figure out

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the preceding word are the ones kept
missing says a letter is taken away from the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A gambler, faced with terrible odds and no expert to help, tries to work out the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' takes letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of Dreadful, giving DEDU; ACE 'missing' A leaves CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to work something out by reasoning, which is the everyday sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: East Fife surprisingly overwhelming noted sides to secure title

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the scrambled letters surround the others
surprisingly says the letters land in an unexpected order
sides takes the outside letters of the word that comes before it

explanation.surface: East Fife, a Scottish football club, surprisingly overpower a notable side to win a title.
explanation.walkthrough: East Fife is a Scottish football club. 'surprisingly' makes FFEI from FIFE, 'overwhelming' ND, from 'sides' of noted.
explanation.definitionFit: An effendi is a Turkish honorific for a man of standing, a courtesy title like sir.

clue.text: Well-informed and bitter? It's probably hot air

parts.note: to be up on something is to be well-informed about it
bitter, the British beer, is often served on draught from the cask

explanation.surface: A pub know-all with a pint of bitter is probably talking hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British beer style typically drawn from the cask on draught.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising current of air is usually warm, since heated air is lighter and climbs, so it is likely hot air.

clue.text: Grace, initially, Henry and I leave his German counterpart

indicators.note: leave says these letters go away from the longer name

parts.note: Heinrich is the German form of the name Henry

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Grace, Henry and the speaker all depart, leaving a German friend behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H of Henry; H and I 'leave' HEINRICH.
explanation.definitionFit: To grace something is to adorn it and add value, which is close to enhancing or improving it.

clue.text: Overlook in accounts numberless Irn-Brus pinched in a hotel

indicators.note: pinched in means held tightly inside the outer letters

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: number gives N, and -less says it is taken out

parts.note: Irn-Bru is a Scottish orange fizzy soft drink; the plural is taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel's books quietly overlook cans of Irn-Bru that guests pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: Irn-Bru is a Scottish soft drink. 'numberless' removes N from IRNBRUS to leave IRBRUS, which is 'pinched in' A and H.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush figures is to touch them up so awkward items vanish, much as one might gloss over them in the books.

clue.text: Battering fish is said to provide protective cover

parts.note: a hiding is a beating, a battering

indicators.note: is said marks a word spoken out loud

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Cooking talk: battered fish, it is claimed, gives a protective coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battering' looks like coating in batter but means a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge where one cannot be found offers shelter, a form of cover from pursuers.

clue.text: Hat with dent in crown felt soft?

definitions.text: Hat with dent in crown felt soft?

parts.words: Hat with dent in crown felt soft?
parts.note: describes a well-known brimmed hat of soft felt with a creased top, while 'felt soft' could read as a sensation

explanation.surface: Someone pressed a dent into their hat's crown and noticed how soft it felt.
explanation.definitionFit: The fedora is a soft felt hat whose crown is creased lengthways, exactly the description given.

clue.text: Sour man who painted Parliament but not the Queen

indicators.note: but not says the following letters are left out

parts.note: J. M. W. Turner painted the burning of the Houses of Parliament in 1834
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: An art-history aside about a grumpy painter of Parliament, with royalty excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner, the English painter, watched Parliament burn in 1834 and painted it. 'but not' drops ER, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that turns goes sour, so the verb means to go off or curdle.

clue.text: Notice tautology?

definitions.meaning: a formal notice of dismissal when a job is cut
saying the same thing twice is needless repetition; the query flags an example

explanation.surface: A two-word puzzle: is a notice a tautology?
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, being made redundant means losing your job because it no longer exists, so a notice of dismissal is a redundancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautology is superfluous repetition, one kind of surplus words; the job sense is a layoff notice.

clue.text: Coming down due to an unexpected bug perhaps fall asleep by the top of the stairs

definitions.text: Coming down due to an unexpected bug perhaps

parts.note: to crash is slang for falling asleep suddenly
the landing is the floor area at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: Someone with a stomach bug collapses asleep at the top of the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests illness but here is a mechanical fault in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency touchdown forced by a fault is an aircraft's abrupt descent, here prompted by an unexpected glitch.

clue.text: Gently does it with piano part

definitions.meaning: to treat something gently, toning it down
the pedal that quietens a piano's sound

explanation.surface: Advice to a pianist: play gently, with the instrument's part.
explanation.definitionFit: The left pedal on a piano mutes it, and figuratively the verb means to play down or handle carefully.

clue.text: Hard breaking into defenceless safe

indicators.note: breaking into says one piece enters the middle of another

parts.note: unarmed means without weapons, defenceless
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough burglar breaks into an unprotected safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' seems to be a strongbox but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming through without injury means being safe and sound, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Tempo flagging according to Spooner in activity that takes place against the clock

definitions.text: activity that takes place against the clock

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: pace is speed or tempo
flagging, drooping from exhaustion, is close to fainting

explanation.surface: A runner's tempo drops off during an event timed against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening letters of PACE and FAINTING gives the two words. 'clock' is slang for face, so painting is done against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock is slang for the human face, so decorating faces with paint is literally done on that surface.

clue.text: Get big problem with leg

parts.note: a catch is a hidden problem or snag
on is the leg side in cricket, the side the batsman's legs face

explanation.surface: A footballer suffers a major problem with his leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion that catches on becomes popular, so to get big is the idiom for spreading in popularity.

clue.text: Clue is second missing first couple of twists

indicators.note: missing says those letters are absent from the longer word

parts.note: in a twinkling means in an instant, a second

indicators.note: first couple of takes the opening two letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A crossword solver complains a clue lacks its first couple of twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first couple of' takes TW from twists, 'missing' from TWINKLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint hint or suspicion of the truth gives a person a lead, much as a clue does.

clue.text: In retrospect some boffin won erudite fame

indicators.note: In retrospect says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking back, a learned scientist won some recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds NWONER across boffin won erudite; 'In retrospect' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean being widely known and celebrated, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Instruction at the Bournville factory how to safeguard recipe?

definitions.text: Instruction at the Bournville factory how to safeguard recipe?

parts.words: Instruction at the Bournville factory how to safeguard recipe?
parts.note: Bournville is Cadbury's chocolate works and also its plain chocolate brand, so the secrecy order doubles as a dark chocolate order

explanation.surface: Factory staff are told how to protect a secret chocolate formula.
explanation.walkthrough: Bournville, near Birmingham, is home to Cadbury's factory and gives its name to a plain dark chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keep a matter secret, the obvious way to protect a recipe, with a dark chocolate pun.

clue.text: Top dog announced

indicators.note: announced says the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: a peke is a Pekinese, a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: The best dog in the show is declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Summit and pinnacle are synonyms of the highest point, which is what top means here.

clue.text: Break down as per projected

indicators.note: projected suggests the letters are thrown out and land rearranged

explanation.surface: A machine breaks down, just as forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break down' looks like a failure but means analysing a sentence; 'projected' scrambles AS PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to analyse it into its grammatical parts, which is a breaking down.

clue.text: Thingummybob emerging from back-to-back parties –- oh dear

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: back-to-back means the second one faces the other way, its back against the first

parts.note: the second party, again a do
ah is an exclamation of dismay

explanation.surface: Someone tired from consecutive parties can't remember the word for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'parties' supplies two DOs; 'back-to-back' turns the second so they meet as DO OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal placeholder words for an item whose name escapes the speaker, like whatsit.

clue.text: Gnomes and imps rage away with the fairies

indicators.note: a person away with the fairies is muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fantasy scene of garden gnomes and imps raging in fairyland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnomes' looks like the little creatures but means short sayings. 'away with the fairies' scrambles IMPS and RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in its literary sense is a pithy maxim, close kin to a short witty saying.

clue.text: Hose only sprinkled borders of nasturtiums

indicators.note: sprinkled means scattered, so the word's letters are scattered
borders of takes the outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A gardener's hosepipe waters only the edges of the nasturtium bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden hosepipe but means stockings. 'sprinkled' turns ONLY into NYLO; 'borders of' gives NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old collective word for stockings and tights, which are commonly made of synthetic fibre.

clue.text: A longing to get settled

parts.note: greed is an excessive longing or desire

explanation.surface: A desire that wants to be satisfied at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something settled has been fixed by consensus, as when terms are decided between two sides.
